sources.observed: USGS NWIS parameter 72279, regularized to 15-minute anchors
sources.seaLevelScenarios: NOAA CO-OPS 2022 Interagency Sea Level Report station projections
sources.localObservedTrend: Great Channel at Stone Harbor monthly means from the same 15-minute archive

method.historic: independent Stone Harbor high-tide peaks separated by at least six hours; a parcel floods only when depth is strictly greater than 0.1 foot above the parcel's highest intersecting original five-foot DEM cell
method.baselineRebase: each observed Stone Harbor peak adjusted to 1 January 2026 using the fitted local observed trend
method.seaLevelCurves: quadratic least-squares fits to each NOAA 2022 median scenario, evaluated annually and rebased to zero in 2026; the observed local trend remains linear
method.cdf: continuous Gaussian-kernel CDF fitted to present-year-rebased independent high-tide peaks
method.uncertainty: two-sided 95 percent calendar-year block-bootstrap percentile interval for the fitted exceedance probability at every elevation, year, and curve
method.future: continuous fitted CDF probability of water level being strictly greater than parcel elevation plus 0.1 foot, with its 95 percent bounds multiplied by 705 expected astronomical high tides per year

floodDefinition.elevationRule: highest original five-foot DEM cell whose center intersects the parcel

observedTrendFit.method: ordinary least squares on equally weighted monthly means from the Stone Harbor 15-minute archive
